decision.headline: This looks like a Coinbase deposit address (not labelled yet, but swept into Coinbase). Recoverable through Coinbase support.

evidence.meaning: Every transfer out of this address went to Coinbase's own wallet — it is swept like a deposit address.
All outflow goes to one counterparty.

warnings: only one sweep seen so far — the address is new; the pattern is consistent but thin

action.title: Support ticket for Coinbase
action.text:
Subject: Funds sent to a Coinbase deposit address by mistake — recovery request

Hello Coinbase support,

On [date] I sent [amount and token] from my wallet [your address] to 0x6465f379a78ad605a9a3f6d3d2abda2ce1bde0e2 on ethereum (transaction [transaction hash]).

This was a mistake. 0x6465f379a78ad605a9a3f6d3d2abda2ce1bde0e2 is a Coinbase customer deposit address — Nansen labels it "🤖 🏦 Coinbase [0xa9d1e0]" and its transfers are swept into Coinbase's own wallets. It may belong to another Coinbase customer, or to an old account of mine. Please locate the account that owns this deposit address and either credit the funds to it (if it is mine) or return them to [your address].

Evidence (Nansen API):
- transaction-with-token-transfer-lookup → token_transfer_array[].to_address_label: 🤖 🏦 Coinbase [0xa9d1e0]
- profiler/address/counterparties → volume_out_usd: 100% of $319 to 0xa9d1…3e43

Account email: [your Coinbase account email]
Thank you,
[your name]
